key_insight: A validated FEM model can generate high-quality synthetic training data, enabling a GNN to predict soft tactile deformation in real time with near-sub-millimetre accuracy.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical workflow for soft sensor design and virtual prototyping when physical data are scarce, expensive, or potentially damaging to collect.
method: Use 82 real camera-tracked contacts only to calibrate and validate the ANSYS FEM model.
Generate 768 synthetic contact scenarios from the validated FEM for GNN training.
Deploy the GNN for fast forward and inverse deformation prediction in a real-time visualization pipeline.
evidence_signal: The validated FEM achieved sub-0.5 mm error in over 90% of validation cases, and the GNN reached 0.32 mm mean absolute error with millisecond inference versus minute-scale FEM simulation.
watch_item: The demonstrated sim-to-real performance is limited to a planar 2D tactile structure, so generalization to more complex 3D sensors or contact conditions still needs confirmation.
paper_title: FEM-Validated Real-Time Modelling of Soft Tactile Deformation
